title: API Access Token Usage
summary: We pass the access token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token for all protected API requests.

content.overview: When making requests to our resource server on behalf of the user, the client includes the access token as a Bearer token in the HTTP Authorization header. The resource server validates the token before returning the requested data.
content.details: We follow the RFC 6750 Bearer Token Usage. The token is obtained from the authorization server after the code exchange. The client adds header: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. This approach keeps tokens out of URLs and request bodies, reducing exposure in logs.
content.examples:
GET /api/userinfo HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer ya29.a0AfH6S...

The server validates the token's signature, expiry, and scopes before responding.
content.caveats: Protect the token in transit with TLS. Token must not be exposed to client-side JavaScript; keep it server-side or in secure storage.
